subject.title: Runtime Self Context: give agents runtime, scale, offload, and cost awareness

question: Should OpenClaw approve the v1 core runtime self-context contract with a top-level runtimeContext config and model-facing runtime tool, narrow it before merge, or defer it behind broader runtime/offload design?
rationale: The source path is clear, but the requested config, prompt exposure modes, tool shape, and plugin/provider ownership boundaries are durable product/API choices that automation should not decide while the implementation PR is still open.

options.title: Approve Or Narrow The First Slice
options.body: Review the linked implementation PR as the contract vehicle, choose the accepted runtimeContext/tool surface, and keep provider refresh plus action execution as explicit follow-ups.

options.title: Defer For Broader Runtime Design
options.body: Keep the issue open but pause the PR until execution placement, offload, cost, and provider hook semantics are reviewed together.

options.title: Reject Core Surface For Now
options.body: Leave environment discovery and plugin-owned APIs as the supported path and close this only if maintainers decide a core runtime self-context layer is not wanted.

recommendation.title: Approve Or Narrow The First Slice
recommendation.body: Review the linked implementation PR as the contract vehicle, choose the accepted runtimeContext/tool surface, and keep provider refresh plus action execution as explicit follow-ups.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter is the strongest current-main history match for the carried-forward prompt/runtime and environment surfaces and was explicitly asked for feedback on the linked contract PR.
